contract: Every command prints one JSON line on stdout: `{"ok":true,"data":...}` on success, or `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"...","message":"...","hint":"..."}}` on failure, and exits 0 or 1. The `hint` names the next step for the `code`; an optional `details` object carries the ids to act on after a partial failure, such as the parts of a thread that could not be deleted. The interactive setup guide and the logs go to stderr, never to stdout.

flags.description: Print the package name and version.
Print the manifest, as help-json does. `<command> --help` prints that command page, as `docs <command>` does.

commands.name: post
commands.summary: Publish a text post, an image, or both, to Threads.
commands.description: Publishes a new post on the account saved in the profile and answers with its id and link. A text over the limit is refused unless --split posts it as a thread of replies. Threads allows 250 posts per 24 hours. Publishing is never retried: a post that timed out may still have gone out, so check the profile before posting again.

options.description: The text of the post, quoted when it contains spaces. Required unless --image is given. 500 characters at most on Threads, an emoji counting its UTF-8 bytes (a thumbs-up is 4).
The profile whose saved account acts. Defaults to "default". A saved token 30 days old or more is refreshed before use. PANDA_SOCIAL_THREADS_TOKEN, when set, overrides the saved token.
A public https URL to a JPEG or PNG image, 8 MB at most. Threads downloads it itself, so a local file must be hosted first.
Post a text over the limit as a thread: the first post, then replies, each answering the one before. If a part fails, the parts already published are deleted.

examples.explanation: Post from the account saved in the default profile.
Post from the account saved in the brand-a profile.

examples.command: panda-social post --to threads --image https://cdn.example.com/cat.jpg --text "A cat on the sofa"
examples.explanation: Post an image with a caption.

examples.command: panda-social post --to threads --text "Release notes that run past 500 characters" --split
examples.explanation: Post a long text as a thread of replies.

commands.output: The new post: `{"platform":"threads","id":"<post id>","url":"<link, or null when Threads did not return one>"}`, plus `"replies":["<id>",...]` for a --split thread.

commands.name: update
commands.summary: Replace a Threads post. Threads has no edit, so --repost deletes it and publishes the new version.
commands.description: Threads cannot edit a published post, so update refuses unless --repost is given. With --repost it deletes the old post first, then publishes the new text or image as post does: the new post gets a new id and link, and the old one takes its likes and replies with it. If the delete fails, nothing is published; if the publish fails after the delete, the error says the old post is gone.

options.description: The platform the post is on.
The numeric id of the post, as post returned it.
The text of the post, quoted when it contains spaces. Required unless --image is given. 500 characters at most on Threads, an emoji counting its UTF-8 bytes (a thumbs-up is 4).
The profile whose saved account acts. Defaults to "default". A saved token 30 days old or more is refreshed before use. PANDA_SOCIAL_THREADS_TOKEN, when set, overrides the saved token.
A public https URL to a JPEG or PNG image, 8 MB at most. Threads downloads it itself, so a local file must be hosted first.
Post a text over the limit as a thread: the first post, then replies, each answering the one before. If a part fails, the parts already published are deleted.
Delete the post and publish the new version. Without it, Threads updates are refused as unsupported.

examples.command: panda-social update --on threads --id 17890000000000001 --text "Hello from panda, typo fixed" --repost
examples.explanation: Replace a post with corrected text.

commands.output: The new post and the id it replaced: `{"platform":"threads","id":"<new id>","url":"<link or null>","replaced":"<old id>"}`, plus `"replies"` for a --split thread.

commands.name: delete
commands.summary: Delete a Threads post by its id.
commands.description: Deletes one post from the account saved in the profile. Replies, the other parts of a --split thread included, are posts of their own: delete each id. Threads allows 100 deletes per 24 hours, and the token needs the threads_delete permission.

options.description: The platform the post is on.
The numeric id of the post, as post returned it.
The profile whose saved account acts. Defaults to "default". A saved token 30 days old or more is refreshed before use. PANDA_SOCIAL_THREADS_TOKEN, when set, overrides the saved token.

examples.explanation: Delete one post from the default profile.

commands.name: setup
commands.summary: Connect a Threads account and save its token under a profile.
commands.description: On a terminal, walks a first-time user through the six one-time steps (a Meta developer account, an app with the Threads API, its permissions, a tester invitation, the token) one at a time, then reads the token without showing it. Without a terminal it answers with the same steps as JSON, for an agent to relay to its human, and the command that finishes the setup. With --token-stdin it reads the token from standard input. Every token is checked with Threads before it is saved in ~/.panda-social/credentials.json, readable by its owner only.

options.description: Read the token from standard input instead of asking for it.
The profile to save the account under. Defaults to "default".

examples.explanation: On a terminal, the guided setup; without one, the steps as JSON.
Save a token piped in on standard input, once Threads confirms it.
Save a second account under the brand-a profile.

commands.output: The connected account, `{"platform":"threads","profile":"<name>","userId":"<id>","username":"<username>"}`. Without a terminal and without --token-stdin, the guide instead: `{"platform":"threads","profile":"<name>","steps":[{"step":1,"title":"...","actions":["..."],"url":"..."}],"finish":"<the command that completes the setup>"}`.

commands.name: status
commands.summary: Check a connected Threads account: whose token it is, how old it is, and how much of the 24-hour quotas is used.
commands.description: Asks Threads whose token the profile holds and reads its rolling 24-hour quotas for posts, replies and deletes. A saved token 30 days old or more is refreshed first, as every Threads command does, so running status now and then keeps an idle token alive: Threads lets a token lapse 60 days after its last refresh, and an expired one needs `panda-social setup threads` again. It never posts.

options.description: The profile whose saved account acts. Defaults to "default". A saved token 30 days old or more is refreshed before use. PANDA_SOCIAL_THREADS_TOKEN, when set, overrides the saved token.

examples.explanation: Check the account saved in the default profile.
Check the account saved in the brand-a profile.

commands.output: The account, its token and its quotas: `{"platform":"threads","profile":"<name>","account":{"userId":"<id>","username":"<username>"},"token":{"source":"saved","savedAt":"<time>","ageDays":<n>,"expiresAt":"<time, or null until the first refresh>","refreshed":<true when this run refreshed it>},"limits":{"posts":{"used":<n>,"total":250,"windowSeconds":86400},"replies":{...},"deletes":{...}}}`. With PANDA_SOCIAL_THREADS_TOKEN set, `token` is `{"source":"environment"}`.

commands.name: help-json
commands.summary: Describe every command, option, example and error code as JSON. Start here.
commands.description: The manifest an agent reads on first contact: the output contract, the global flags, every command with its usage line, parameters, examples and error codes, and the next step for every error code. The same manifest ships as docs/commands.json.

examples.explanation: Read the whole command surface in one call.

commands.name: docs
commands.summary: Show one command's full documentation as markdown.
commands.description: The long form of one command: what it does, its usage line, every parameter, examples ready to paste into a shell, its output and its error codes. docs/COMMANDS.md collects every page.

errors.hint: The setup stopped before a token was pasted. Run `panda-social setup threads` again when you have it.
The credentials file is not valid. Fix or delete ~/.panda-social/credentials.json, then run `panda-social setup threads`.

The token lacks a permission this action needs: threads_delete to delete, threads_manage_replies for --split. Add it under Use cases, Access the Threads API, Customize, generate a new token, and run `panda-social setup threads` again.
Threads could not download or read the image. Check that the URL opens in a private browser window and serves a JPEG or PNG of 8 MB at most, then retry.
Threads needs a public https URL to a JPEG or PNG image, 8 MB at most. Host a local file first, then pass its URL with --image.
Pass the numeric id that post returned, for example --id 17890000000000001.
Use lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter or digit, 40 characters at most. Example: --profile brand-a
Connect an account with `panda-social setup threads` (add `--profile <name>` for another profile), or set PANDA_SOCIAL_THREADS_TOKEN.
Pass the text of the post with --text (quoted when it contains spaces), an image URL with --image, or both.
graph.threads.net could not be reached. Check the network, then retry.
Set HOME (USERPROFILE on Windows), or pass the token in PANDA_SOCIAL_THREADS_TOKEN instead of saving it.
Threads allows 250 posts and 100 deletes per 24 hours. Wait, then retry.
Threads rejected the request; the message says why. Fix what it names (the text, the image URL or the post id), then retry.
Threads was still processing the image after 60 seconds, so nothing was published. Retry the post.
Threads allows 500 characters per post, an emoji counting its UTF-8 bytes. Shorten the text, or pass --split to post it as a thread of replies.
Threads did not answer in time, so the post or the delete may still have gone through: check the profile before retrying.
Threads refused the token. Generate a new one (Meta app dashboard, Use cases, Access the Threads API, Settings, User Token Generator) and run `panda-social setup threads` again.
Quote any value that contains spaces, for example --text "Hello from panda".
Run `panda-social help-json` for every command, or `panda-social docs <command>` for one.
Run `panda-social docs <command>` for the options that command takes.
Threads is the only platform so far: name threads, as the command examples show.
The credentials file could not be read. Check that ~/.panda-social/credentials.json belongs to you.
Threads cannot edit a published post. Pass --repost to delete it and publish the new version: it gets a new id and link, and loses its likes and replies.
The token could not be saved. Check that your home folder is writable, then run the setup again.
